text.visual_description: In the image, a seal pup serves as the main character, depicted against a neutral, sandy background. The seal's head is slightly tilted, creating an endearing and somewhat comical appearance.
text.usage_text: Awkward Moment Seal is an advice animal image macro series featuring a seal with a wide-eyed expression and captions describing socially awkward or uncomfortable situations in a similar vein to "That Awkward Moment…" and Socially Awkward Penguin.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image is a close-up of a mallard duck peacefully floating on a body of water. There are no other characters or entities present, and the duck itself is not engaged in any action beyond a serene glide across the water’s surface.
text.usage_text: Actual Advice Mallard is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a male wild duck accompanied by captions containing life hacks and other useful information.

text.visual_description: The scene centers around a bear cub resting its head and front paws on a log. The bear has a contemplative expression with its eyes looking forward, creating a focal point on the facial expression.
text.usage_text: Confession Bear is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a Malayan sun bear leaning against a log. The images are captioned with confessions about taboo behaviors and controversial opinions that are often kept secret for fear of being ostracized.

text.visual_description: The scene core features an older man with a distinguished appearance, characterized by a white beard and hair, wearing a dark suit. The man appears to be indoors, with a blurred background suggesting an office setting.
text.usage_text: George Zimmer copypasta is a series of anecdotal stories that are narrated in the voice of the founder and CEO of the U.S. clothing retailer Men's Wearhouse. Examples of the series detail Zimmer's machismo and sexual escapades with colorful sexual metaphors. Similar to Billy Mays copypasta, each story typically begins with his TV commercial tagline "Hi, I'm George Zimmer, founder and CEO of the Men's Wearhouse" and always ends with "I GUARANTEE IT."

text.visual_description: The image features a prominently displayed wolf's head at the center, appearing fierce and aggressive. Its mouth is wide open, showcasing sharp teeth, as if in a snarl or roar.
text.usage_text: Insanity Wolf is like the mentally disturbed cousin of Courage Wolf and is placed in the God Tier category on Memegenerator.net. While Courage Wolf often encourages people to overcome life's obstacles, Insanity Wolf tells his viewers to rape, kill, and commit other acts of insanity. There is even a Facebook app for Insanity Wolf.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a penguin prominently positioned in the center, walking awkwardly across a contrasting background divided into quadrants of red and blue. There is no visible text in the image as presented, but the background's layout suggests space for additional commentary, typically a setup-punchline format seen in such templates.
text.usage_text: Socially Awkward Penguin is an advice animal image macro series featuring a penguin lacking both social skills and self-esteem. The text typically narrates uncomfortable life situations, highlighting an exceptionally clumsy or inelegant response.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a young boy standing in front of a microwave, which is open and empty. The boy's expression suggests a pause or contemplation, and he is wearing a gray polo shirt.
text.usage_text: Minor Advice Marvin is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a young boy staring blankly into the distance, with various captions detailing everyday episodes of regrettable mistakes that can unfold as a result of one's own oversight.

text.visual_description: The image features a young child, prominently positioned in the center against a background of overlapping, colorful triangles. The child is wearing a green and white shirt and is making a fist with one hand while the rest of the body is not visible.
text.usage_text: Success Kid, sometimes known as I Hate Sandcastles, is a reaction image of a baby at a beach with a smug facial expression. It has been used in image macros to designate either success or frustration. In early 2011, the original image was turned into an advice animal style image macro with captions describing a situation that goes better than expected.

text.visual_description: The image features a close-up of a seal with its eyes closed. The seal's facial expression suggests an action of relaxation or contentment.
text.usage_text: Seal of Approval, also known as Satisfied Seal, is an advice animal image macro series featuring a close-up photograph of a seal with captions containing anecdotes about various gratifying experiences.

text.visual_description: The scene core features an adorable young wolf pup sitting in a field filled with blossoming pink wildflowers. The pup is looking upwards, mouth slightly open, as if focused on a small insect flying above it.
text.usage_text: Baby Insanity Wolf is an advice animal image macro series based on a photograph of a wolf cub howling and various captions describing small acts of defiance, often perceptible only to the person carrying them out, in a similar vein to those highlighted in "Thug Life" remixes.

text.visual_description: The image features a single young man reclining against what appears to be a wooden or cushioned surface, possibly a headboard or couch. His eyes are half-open, his head slightly tilted, and his mouth slightly open in a lopsided grin.
text.usage_text: [10] Guy (also known as "Really High Guy" and "Stoner Stanley") is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a young man who appears to be under the influence of marijuana. The captions typically portray stereotypical stoner behavior, similar to Stoner Dog, such as giving invalid answers to misunderstood questions and craving junk food. In April 2021, UK-based resident Connor Sinclair revealed himself to be the man depicted in 10 Guy after nearly a decade of anonymity.

text.visual_description: The image shows a woman in formal attire standing against a backdrop featuring an American flag. She is wearing a dark blazer and an orange top, with her hair neatly styled.
text.usage_text: Hillary Clinton is an American politician who served as the First Lady of the United States from 1993 to 2001, Senator of New York from 2001 to 2009, and the 67th Secretary of State from 2009 to 2013. A longtime member of the Democratic Party, Clinton has run twice for the presidency of the United States, first as a candidate in the 2008 Democratic primaries and later as the Democratic nominee in the 2016 general election.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a group of animated characters in a construction site or similar outdoor setting. The main character, in the foreground, is dressed as a superhero with a distinctive large eye symbol on the chest, wearing a red and yellow costume with a cape.
text.usage_text: Captain Hindsight is an image macro series based on the eponymous superhero character originally featured in an episode of the animated TV series South Park. Inspired by the character, image captions generally present various types of predicaments and then lecture on what could've been done differently to avoid the situation altogether (see also: Captain Obvious).

text.visual_description: The image features a character wearing round, reflective sunglasses and a leather jacket, standing in an urban environment. The reflections in the sunglasses show two different scenes, suggesting a contrast or choice.
text.usage_text: Matrix Morpheus is an advice animal image macro series featuring a screen capture of the fictional character Morpheus (played by Laurence Fishburne) from The Matrix franchise. The captions typically follow a two-line format with the first line reading "What if I Told You," followed by a revelation that often belittles futile or petty behavior, in a similar vein to the advice animal characters Conspiracy Keanu and Sudden Clarity Clarence.

text.visual_description: The image features a young woman as the main character, standing in what appears to be a public setting. She is wearing a colorful, knitted hat and has long dreadlocks.
text.usage_text: College Liberal is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a young Caucasian female with dreadlocks wearing a knitted cap. The captions typically portray the character as a naive and hypocritical left-wing political activist, referencing various clichés associated with the hippie subculture.

name: So I Got That Goin For Me Which Is Nice

text.visual_description: The image features a single character wearing a camouflage bucket hat and a plain shirt, standing outside. There's a background with a building and some trees, giving the setting a rural or outdoor feel.
text.usage_text: "So I Got That Goin' For Me, Which Is Nice" is an advice animal image macro series featuring a screen capture of the character Carl Spackler (played by Bill Murray) from the 1980 comedy film Caddyshack. The captions usually begin with a sentence revealing a personal problem or ordeal, followed by a notion of a silver lining and the original quote from Caddyshack in verbatim.

text.visual_description: The scene features an adult male character with short hair and a beard, dressed in a beige shirt and a striped tie, appearing indoors in a likely office setting. He is slightly hunched over, suggesting engagement in conversation or listening intently.
text.usage_text: "Afraid to Ask" Andy is an advice animal image macro series featuring a still image of Andy Dwyer (played by Chris Pratt), one of the main characters from the American TV sitcom Parks and Recreation, captioned with various confessions of one's ignorance in current events or common knowledge, followed by the phrase "…and at this point I’m afraid to ask.”

text.visual_description: The scene depicts an older man sitting in a horse-drawn cart, possibly in a rural setting as indicated by the surrounding landscape that includes hills and trees. He is wearing a straw hat, glasses, and traditional clothing.
text.usage_text: Pepperidge Farm Remembers is an image macro series based on a tagline used in an advertisement for the commercial bakery Pepperidge Farm. The series features a still shot from a parody of the commercial, as seen in the animated television series Family Guy, and captions reminiscing about outdated relics and practices from past decades.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts an office setting with a male character seated directly in front of a computer. He is dressed in a dark suit and tie, giving a formal and professional appearance.
text.usage_text: "And It's Gone!" (also known as "Aaaand It's Gone") is an advice animal image macro series featuring a picture of a bank teller from the animated television show South Park. The image macros are often accompanied by captions describing lost opportunities or items, ending in the titular phrase "And it's gone."

text.visual_description: The image features a middle-aged man in a typical office environment, wearing a light blue dress shirt, red suspenders, a patterned tie, and glasses. He appears to be standing in a cubicle-filled office with a coffee mug in hand.
text.usage_text: "That Would Be Great" is an image macro series featuring the character Bill Lumbergh from the 1999 comedy film Office Space. The captions typically mimic the character's non-confrontational speech with various requests ending with the expression "That'd be great."

text.visual_description: The scene features a single individual, an elderly man dressed in a formal suit with a distinct white beard and glasses, standing against a blue curtain backdrop. He has one arm raised emphatically, holding a marker or pen in his gloved hand, while the other hand appears to be holding papers.
text.usage_text: "The Rent is Too Damn High" is a political slogan adopted by Jimmy McMillan, a New York City resident and founder of the Rent Is Too Damn High Party, who ran for New York’s state gubernatorial election in November 2010. McMillan's catchphrase has inspired the snowclone template “The X is too damn high,” which is often featured in an Advice Animal image macro series featuring a photo of McMillan from the night of the gubernatorial debate.

text.visual_description: The image displays a classroom setting featuring a female teacher standing in front of a world map and a chalkboard. The teacher is gesturing toward the viewer with one hand extended, giving the impression she is inviting or encouraging them to join the learning process.
text.usage_text: Unhelpful High School Teacher is an advice animal image macro series featuring a stock photo of a woman standing in front of a map of the world and a chalkboard. The captioned text describes lazy or irresponsible teaching methods, as well as cliché expressions and retorts frequently used by teachers in interacting with students.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts an older man seated and holding a paper or card, intently looking at it as if reading or preparing to reveal something important. The visible text on the card includes the name "maury," indicating some sort of official or notable document.
text.usage_text: Maury Lie Detector, also known as The Lie Detector Determined That Was a Lie, is an advice animal image macro series featuring a screen-captured image of the Maury tabloid talk show host Maury Povich, with captions presenting various claims as fabrications. The series plays off a recurring theme involving the use of lie detectors on the show, in a similar vein to the You Are Not The Father image macro series mocking the show's frequent paternity testing.

name: The Most Interesting Man In The World

text.visual_description: The image features a well-dressed, bearded man seated at a table with his arm resting on it, pointing slightly, with a bottle of Dos Equis beer beside him. The man is wearing a black suit with a white shirt and has a confident posture, suggesting a sophisticated environment, possibly a bar or lounge setting.
text.usage_text: The Most Interesting Man in the World is an advice animal character inspired by the titular protagonist of the highly successful advertising campaign for the Dos Equis beer brand that ran from 2006 to 2018. In the image macro series, the character is depicted as a highly charismatic and well-traveled gentleman with refined tastes in many things, much like the nameless bearded man originally portrayed in the campaign, often accompanied by captions based on the phrasal template "I don't always X, but when I do, I Y."

name: Am I The Only One Around Here

text.visual_description: The scene features a robust man wearing tinted glasses and a vest, brandishing a handgun in a bowling alley-like setting. His expression is stern and focused, contributing to a tense atmosphere.
text.usage_text: Am I the Only One Around Here (also known as "Angry Walter") is an advice animal image macro series featuring a screenshot of the character Walter Sobchak (played by John Goodman) drawing a gun in the 1998 comedy film "The Big Lebowski." The captions often convey the feeling that the poster is alone in holding an unpopular opinion.

text.visual_description: The image features a single penguin positioned centrally on a background divided into blue segments creating a radial pattern. The penguin is captured mid-stride, suggesting movement or action such as walking or dancing.
text.usage_text: Socially Awkward Penguin is an advice animal image macro series featuring a penguin lacking both social skills and self-esteem. The text typically narrates uncomfortable life situations, highlighting an exceptionally clumsy or inelegant response.

text.visual_description: The image features an older man with a white beard, wearing a hooded cloak, set against a desert-like backdrop. He appears to be gazing into the distance, possibly at something or someone out of frame.
text.usage_text: Obi-Wan Kenobi, also known as Ben Kenobi, is a fictional character from the Star Wars series of films, television shows, comic books, and other forms of media. In the films, Kenobi portrays the Jedi master or trainer of Anakin and Luke Skywalker, the protagonists of the original Star Wars trilogy and prequel trilogy, respectively. Online, Obi-Wan, as portrayed by Ewan McGregor, has been the inspiration for numerous Prequel Memes, which focus on the Star Wars prequel trilogy of films.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a woman sitting in what appears to be an airplane or a similar vehicle, focusing intently on her smartphone. She is wearing dark sunglasses, which obscure her eyes, but her posture and the set of her mouth suggest concentration.
text.usage_text: Texts From Hillary is a single-topic blog featuring a series of vertical, multi-pane image macros based on a photograph of United States Secretary of State Hillary Clinton sitting aboard a military aircraft while wearing sunglasses and reading from her smartphone.

text.visual_description: The image features a serene scene of a male duck with vibrant plumage floating on calm water. There are no other characters or entities present, and the duck is positioned centrally, creating a focal point in the image.
text.usage_text: Malicious Advice Mallard is a derivative of Actual Advice Mallard. While Actual Advice Mallard sends out life hacks and great info, Malicious Advice Mallard sends out advice that, if used, later makes you realize you should be ashamed of what you did.

text.visual_description: The scene centers around a penguin positioned diagonally across a background divided into two contrasting color triangles, blue on the top half and red on the bottom. The penguin appears to be in motion, suggesting a hasty or awkward movement, with one foot slightly raised and wings outstretched in what could be a balancing attempt.
text.usage_text: Socially Awkward Penguin is an advice animal image macro series featuring a penguin lacking both social skills and self-esteem. The text typically narrates uncomfortable life situations, highlighting an exceptionally clumsy or inelegant response.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template consists of a sequence of four images depicting a human head, each with increasingly elaborate and illuminated brains. There are no textual elements present in the template itself, although it is often used with added text to create humorous or satirical commentary.
text.usage_text: Galaxy Brain, also known as Expanding Brain, is a multi-panel exploitable image series comparing the brain size of a person relative to other variables. Though the expanding brain is usually implied to showcase intellectual superiority over various objects, it is more often used in an ironic sense to imply the opposite, where objects of derision are implied to be of higher standard than objects that are usually highly regarded. For example, when used with Whomst, a person who uses "who" will be shown with the smallest brain, while a person who uses the most ridiculous variation, i.e., "whomst'd've," will be shown with the largest brain.

text.visual_description: The scene features two animated characters, a cowboy and a space ranger, in a room with a plain backdrop, adorned with a few star stickers. The cowboy character stands to the left, appearing uneasy, with his mouth slightly open and eyebrows raised.
text.usage_text: X, X Everywhere is a phrasal template typically used for a wide range of cultural references, from quotable lines heard in popular films and TV shows to more obscure things found in viral videos and games. Many instances of "X Everywhere" may be seen as an indicator for emerging trends, while some should be read as a grievance or complaint against them, depending on the context.

text.visual_description: The scene centers around a man seated at a table set up outdoors in a park-like setting. He appears relaxed, leaning back in his chair with one leg crossed over the other, casually holding a cup as if enjoying a drink.
text.usage_text: Steven Crowder's "Change My Mind" Campus Sign is a photograph of American-Canadian conservative podcaster Steven Crowder seated behind a sign that reads "Male Privilege is a myth / Change My Mind" outside of Texas Christian University. Since its upload via Crowder's Twitter account in February 2018, the photograph has been turned into an exploitable template for online parodies.

text.visual_description: The central scene features a man with long hair and a beard, dressed in medieval-style clothing. He is captured mid-sentence with his right hand raised, fingers forming a small circle, a gesture indicating precision or emphasis.
text.usage_text: "One Does Not Simply Walk Into Mordor" (snowclone: "One Does Not Simply X into Mordor") is a memorable quote from the 2001 fantasy epic film Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring. Variants of the phrase are often used in image macros featuring Mordor, a fictional location from The Lord of the Rings franchise, or the character Boromir, who originally says the line in the film.

text.visual_description: The scene features a crowded group of young people at what appears to be a concert or festival. The central figure, a young man, stands out with a surprised and slightly bewildered expression.
text.usage_text: Sudden Clarity Clarence is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a young man at a party staring into the distance as if he is experiencing an epiphany. The captions often contain the phrase "Oh my God" or "Holy Shit" followed by a sudden realization that is trivial and insignificant. The series has been criticized for being redundant due to its similarities to Conspiracy Keanu, featuring an image of a frightened-looking Keanu Reeves.

text.visual_description: The image portrays a group of young children, seemingly in a playful or celebratory setting. They are shown with joyful expressions and dynamic poses, suggesting movement or dance.
text.usage_text: Third World Success is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a dancing tribal child with captions about overcoming hardships that are associated with life in underdeveloped countries. The series can be seen as a derivative of Success Kid and the antithesis of First World Problems.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single animated character with distinctive orange hair and a slightly squinted expression. The character is seen from the shoulders up, wearing a red jacket over a white shirt.
text.usage_text: Futurama Fry is an image macro series that uses a still of Fry squinting his eyes from the TV show Futurama and is typically paired with overlaid text using a phrasal template. The top line reads "Not sure if X," with "or just Y" as the bottom line, and is used to represent an internal monologue.

text.visual_description: The image features a cartoon character in a bright red ski instructor outfit holding ski poles and standing in a snowy landscape. The main character has wide eyes and an open mouth, suggesting he is speaking or exclaiming.
text.usage_text: Super Cool Ski Instructor is an advice animal image macro series featuring a picture of the ski instructor Thumper from the animated sitcom South Park. The macros are accompanied by captions advising against risky or impetuous behaviors, followed by the warning, "You're gonna have a bad time."

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a woman indoors, seated on a striped chair. She is holding an orange fruit to her ear, seemingly mimicking a phone call, with her tongue playfully extended in a humorous action.
text.usage_text: Wrong Number Rita features the image of a teenage girl holding an orange to her face, resembling the way a person would answer the phone. She has a dumbfounded look on her face, appearing as though she is unsure of what is going on. Most captions of this image have to do with Rita asking dumb questions about phones and technology.

text.visual_description: The image features a stylized depiction of a dinosaur, often referred to as a velociraptor. The dinosaur is holding one of its clawed fingers up to its chin, suggesting a contemplative or pondering pose.
text.usage_text: Philosoraptor is an advice animal image macro series featuring an illustration of a Velociraptor paired with captions depicting the dinosaur as being deeply immersed in metaphysical inquiries or unraveling quirky paradoxes.

text.visual_description: The image features a two-panel comparison scene with a man in a bright orange puffer jacket against a monochromatic background. In the top panel, he is turning away with a hand raised, suggesting rejection.
text.usage_text: Drakeposting refers to the practice of posting reaction images and other still shots from the music video of the Canadian hip hop artist's 2015 hit single "Hotline Bling" on the imageboard site 4chan, typically to express one's disdain of the thread topic or something said by another poster in a similar vein to the usage of Costanza.jpg.

text.visual_description: The scene features a highway exit scenario comprised of two main elements: a road sign and a car. The road sign includes directions indicating a "Left" exit (Exit 12), while the image below depicts a car sharply veering off to the right, leaving visible skid marks on the road.
text.usage_text: Left Exit 12 Off Ramp is a series of exploitables in which a car swerves into an off-ramp. On the highway sign, the meme's author photoshops something the author disapproves of and something they would prefer. The car swerves toward the preference.

text.visual_description: The image consists of two panels featuring a puppet character with reddish-brown fur and wide eyes. It appears to be facing forward in the first panel and slightly turning its head away in the second.
text.usage_text: Awkward Look Monkey Puppet refers to two images of the Monkey Puppet known as Kenta from the Japanese children's television show Ōkiku Naru Ko awkwardly looking towards the camera and then away. The side-eye glance is not the original scene of the monkey and was instead created in Photoshop when the meme was first made in 2016. The double image gained significant popularity as a reaction in 2019 after originally circulating in Spanish meme communities in the years prior.

text.visual_description: The image features a yellow, sponge-like character with large, expressive eyes and a wide, open-mouth smile. The character is holding its hands up with fingers splayed, and there is a rainbow arc extending from one hand to the other with sparkles, creating an imaginative scene.
text.usage_text: Imagination refers to a series of drawn images and image macros, mostly known on DeviantArt and Memegenerator. Most of the pictures show various fictional characters being in a cardboard box, posing with straightened-up arms and a rainbow shining from the left hand to the right hand, while the term "Imagination" or other terms are shown.

text.visual_description: The image features a single character who is dressed in a superhero costume, seated behind an office desk. There are no specific actions taking place, as the character appears to be sitting calmly.
text.usage_text: Masturbating Spider-Man is a series of image macros of an edited screenshot taken from the '60s Spider-Man series, showing Spider-Man sitting on a desk. In a similar vein to other advice animals like Bear Grylls, the bottom caption normally remains consistent, being "And I'm Just Sitting Here Masturbating," the one featured on most of the macros.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a seagull perched on a green rooftop. The sequence of images captures the seagull in different stages of vocalization, progressing from a calm, closed beak to an open-mouthed scream, with the final image dramatically altered to a bright red background with glowing eyes.
text.usage_text: Inhaling Seagull is an exploitable two-panel image macro series featuring a photograph of a seagull leaning backwards followed by a picture of the seagull squawking forwards. The first image is captioned with the word "inhales," while the second image is typically captioned with verbose copypastas and song lyrics.

text.visual_description: The scene is divided into two panels. In the first panel, a hand is reaching towards two red buttons on a control panel, creating a decision point.
text.usage_text: "Daily Struggle" is an exploitable comic featuring a character attempting to push one of two red buttons labeled with contradicting statements.

text.visual_description: The scene features a cartoon character resembling a small, yellow creature with pointy ears, red cheeks, and an open mouth. This character is presenting a surprised expression.
text.usage_text: Surprised Pikachu, also known as Shocked Pikachu, refers to a screenshot from the Pokémon anime of the character Pikachu with its mouth agape, as though it were surprised at something. In the autumn of 2018, the image was used as a reaction image paired with captions where a set-up leads to a predictable outcome that nevertheless leaves one surprised.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this template features a simplistic structure with two unfilled sections divided by a vertical line under the prominent text "WHO WOULD WIN?" This layout suggests an impending comparison or competition between two entities, setting the stage for engaging content to be inserted. The key visual element is the clean, minimalistic separation which invites viewers to anticipate a contrast or contest, making it versatile for numerous creative uses.
text.usage_text: Who Would Win? is an image macro series posing the question "Who would win?" in various hypothetical battles between two opposing subjects.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a cartoon character with wide, exaggerated eyes and a gaping mouth, holding a broom or mop in an energetic pose. The character is wearing a pink outfit, and the background is dominated by bright, jagged yellow lines suggesting explosive energy or intense emotion.
text.usage_text: All the Things, sometimes known as all the Y, is a snowclone and exploitable cartoon used to make a hyperbolic statement about performing an action. The person in the original comic panel is often manipulated to appear as a different character. (See also: fsjal)

text.visual_description: The scene is divided into three panels featuring two main characters: a young boy and an adult man, both dressed formally. In the first panel, the boy is looking up at the man with wide eyes, suggesting he might be asking a question or seeking reassurance.
text.usage_text: Finding Neverland is an image macro series featuring three screen-captured panels depicting a conversation between the characters Barrie (played by Johnny Depp) and Peter (played by Freddie Highmore) in the 2004 drama film Finding Neverland. The first panel features a teary-eyed Peter announcing why he's upset, followed by a panel of Barrie looking at him sympathetically and a final panel in which the two embrace.

text.visual_description: The scene features two main characters: a futuristic-looking robot wearing a white fur coat and holding a ring, and a green-skinned humanoid figure in the background. The robot appears to be in the foreground, engaging in a gesture that draws attention, with an expression that emphasizes determination or assertiveness.
text.usage_text: "I'm going to build my own theme park with blackjack and hookers" is a memorable quote said by Bender in a 1999 episode of the animated TV series Futurama. In image macros and comments, variations of the phrasal template "We'll create our own (X) with blackjack and hookers" have been used to express dissatisfaction with the status quo, suggesting that the commenter could do it better.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single bird, known as a potoo, with prominent large yellow eyes that stand out vividly against the dark background. The bird is facing forward, seemingly making direct eye contact with the viewer, which creates a striking focal point.
text.usage_text: Weird Stuff I Do Potoo, also known as Peculiar Potoo, is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a potoo bird accompanied by captions confessing strange idiosyncrasies and other unique behaviors.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a close-up image of a young person with shaggy hair and a startled expression. There are no additional characters or visible text in the image.
text.usage_text: Conspiracy Keanu is an advice animal image macro series featuring a still photo of the Hollywood actor Keanu Reeves wearing a frightened expression from the 1989 comedy film Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure. The images are typically captioned with paranoid conjectures and absurdly philosophical questions that bear similarities to the Paranoid Parrot, Philosoraptor, and Stoner Dog advice animal series.

text.visual_description: The scene features an elderly woman sitting in front of a laptop. She is adjusting her glasses with one hand while leaning slightly forward, suggesting she is trying to get a better look at the screen.
text.usage_text: Grandma Finds the Internet, also known as Internet Grandma Surprise, is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of an elderly woman looking at a laptop computer screen with captions expressing shock and bewilderment by what she discovers online. The captions often imply she is a naive Internet user who reacts to famous videos, shock sites, ads, and spam in a similar vein to Net Noob and First Day on the Internet Kid.

text.visual_description: The image showcases a man standing outside, touching his temple with a confident gesture. He wears a black leather jacket and a gold watch.
text.usage_text: Roll Safe is an image macro series featuring a screenshot of actor Kayode Ewumi grinning and pointing to his temple while portraying the character Reece Simpson (a.k.a. "Roll Safe") in the web series Hood Documentary. The images are often captioned with various jokes mocking poor decision-making and failures in critical thinking.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts an office meeting with four main characters seated around a conference table. In the first panel, three individuals are on one side, seemingly conversing with a man seated alone on the opposite side.
text.usage_text: Boardroom Suggestion is an exploitable comic series satirizing the perception gap between what consumers want and what corporate executives think they want, in a similar vein to Corporate Logic and All Right, Gentlemen comics. Each comic begins with the executive consulting his staff for new product ideas, followed by the first two employees giving corporate-safe answers, which ends abruptly with the third employee being thrown out of the window for suggesting a consumer-approved idea.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a single person dressed in formal attire, wearing a dark suit, a yellow shirt, and a patterned tie. The background is composed of a radial gradient of various brown shades, which is often used to draw attention to the central figure.
text.usage_text: Successful Black Man is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a black man dressed in business attire, superimposed in front of a brown and beige color wheel background. The jokes typically employ a bait-and-switch format, with the top caption appearing to set up a stereotype about African Americans, followed by a bottom caption rendering the phrase innocuous, in a similar vein to the Ordinary Muslim Man advice animal character.

text.visual_description: The scene features a close-up of a gray cartoon cat with its eyes widened, tilting its head slightly. The character's eyes are notably large with prominent yellow irises and small, black pupils, giving a startled or shocked appearance.
text.usage_text: Unsettled Tom, also known as Traumatized Tom and Concerned Tom, refers to a Paint drawing of character Tom from the cartoon series Tom and Jerry wearing an expression of concern. Originating from a Tails Gets Trolled comic and circulated as a reaction image on 4chan, in March 2019 the picture gained popularity on Reddit, often used in reference to shocking behavior.

text.visual_description: The image consists of three panels depicting a conversation within a vehicle. The first panel shows a man driving, speaking towards the passenger seat; his facial expression suggests he is asking a question or making a statement.
text.usage_text: The Rock Driving is a multi-pane exploitable image series based on several screen-captured images from the 2009 family adventure film Race to Witch Mountain. The comics usually begin with the film's protagonist Jack asking Sara a question while driving, to which she responds with a shocking revelation that makes Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson turn his head with a startled facial expression.

text.visual_description: The image is a three-panel collage featuring a solitary character, a man with a mustache, short, curly dark hair, and casual clothing. In the top panel, he is sitting on a swing in a garden, appearing deep in thought and disconnected from his surroundings.
text.usage_text: Pablo Escobar Waiting, also known as Sad Pablo Escobar, is a series of three-panel image macros featuring the character Pablo Escobar (played by Wagner Moura) from the Netflix series Narcos, staring blankly in three different screen captures from the series. The meme expresses the sadness and boredom associated with anticipation.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a joyful woman standing in an expansive, flower-filled field with a backdrop of majestic mountains. She is dressed in a classic blue dress and apron and has her arms outspread as if twirling or embracing the scenery.
text.usage_text: Look at all the fucks I give is a catchphrase often used in image macros and animated GIFs to show how little one cares about what someone else is talking about. Similar to "Cool Story Bro" and "Not a Single Fuck Was Given That Day," it is a sarcastic iteration of the colloquial phrase "I don't give a fuck" and the images usually feature someone standing with his/her arms wide open.

text.visual_description: The image features two parts. In the top half, two blank sheets of paper are displayed side by side, held by a person whose face is not visible.
text.usage_text: They're The Same Picture is a two-panel exploitable meme based on a scene from the television series The Office in which the character Pam presents two pictures before Pam says they're the same picture in the second panel.

text.visual_description: The scene features two main characters sitting in the foreground, dressed in extravagant, eye-catching outfits, one holding a small dog. The character on the left has a flamboyant appearance with highly stylized bleached hair and a red and silver outfit, while the character on the right sports a sleek black bob hairstyle and an equally striking red dress.
text.usage_text: X is so hot right now is a memorable quote uttered by the character Mugatu in the 2001 comedy film Zoolander. Online, people use the phrase to describe something that is trending or popular in image macros that feature a shot from the film in which Mugatu says the line.

text.visual_description: The image shows a heated argument between two main characters, a muscular older man with a gray mustache and a younger man wearing a black cap. The older man, sitting at a desk, is yelling and pointing, while the younger man responds with equal intensity, gesturing aggressively.
text.usage_text: American Chopper Argument refers to a scene from the American reality TV show American Chopper in which Paul Teutul Sr. and Paul Teutul Jr. get in a shouting match about Jr.'s tardiness. Since its original airing in 2009, the explosive scene has spawned an exploitable photocomic series that humorously illustrates various debates in pop culture fandom. In March 2018, the meme made its first breakout on Twitter.

text.visual_description: The scene includes three geometric shapes, each with a corresponding label beneath it. At the top left is a pentagon, labeled "Pentagon," featuring five sides.
text.usage_text: Pentagon Hexagon Octagon is an exploitable series featuring three shapes and one image of something with the suffix "-gon."

text.visual_description: The image consists of two juxtaposed scenes. On the left, there are two women; the one in the foreground is visibly upset, with her mouth open as if shouting, and is pointing towards something off-screen.
text.usage_text: Woman Yelling at a Cat (not to be confused with Screaming Cat) refers to a meme format featuring a screencap of The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills cast members Taylor Armstrong and Kyle Richards, followed by a picture of a confused-looking cat sitting behind a dinner plate. The format gained significant popularity across the web in mid-June 2019, and the cat was later identified as Smudge the Cat.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single male character, adorned in what appears to be a Roman-inspired outfit with decorative elements, including a headband and ornate pins on his chest. The character's arm is extended outward, with his thumb pointing downward, a gesture commonly associated with disapproval or rejection.
text.usage_text: Downvoting Roman / Commodus Thumbs Down is an Advice Animal-style image macro series featuring a still shot of actor Joaquin Phoenix as Emperor Commodus in the 2000 epic film Gladiator. The image depicts a stone-faced Commodus giving a thumbs down, and the overlaid text usually conveys dissatisfaction towards a post on a website or forum where a voting system is present, especially on Reddit.

text.visual_description: The image features two well-known comic book characters in a dynamic, tense scene. One character is depicted slapping the other across the face.
text.usage_text: Batman Slapping Robin, also known as "My Parents Are Dead," is an exploitable image of the DC Comics superhero Batman slapping his protégé Robin in mid-conversation. Taken from a comic book published in 1965, the single-panel illustration has inspired a series of parodies featuring custom-captioned speech bubbles on 4chan, Reddit, and elsewhere.

text.visual_description: The image features a formally dressed man in a tuxedo holding up a glass, suggesting a toast. The background is blurry with lights, creating a festive atmosphere.
text.usage_text: Great Gatsby Reaction or Leonardo DiCaprio Toast refers to a series of reaction images and GIFs featuring actor Leonardo DiCaprio as Jay Gatsby toasting a martini glass from the 2013 film The Great Gatsby. Typically, the reaction is used to show agreement or praise for something, but it is also used as an image macro in memes.

text.visual_description: The scene features a woman seated with her arms wrapped around her knees, wearing casual clothing. She is positioned against a colorful, segmented background with blue, green, red, and purple sections emanating outward.
text.usage_text: Sheltering Suburban Mom is an advice animal image macro series satirizing the stereotype of a suburban, overprotective mother who fails to practice what she preaches to her children. The series became widespread through advice animal hub sites like Quickmeme and Reddit's subreddit.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a prominent hand situated mid-action, poised to slap a large, prominently displayed blue button. There are no characters in the conventional sense, as the focus is solely on the interaction between the hand and the button.
text.usage_text: Nut Button refers to an image of a hand going to hit a blue button, badly edited to have the word "NUT" on it. The image often has text above it, usually "When you're hitting it from behind and she turns around and moans 'X'," or something similar. Over the course of 2016, it evolved such that "nut" was replaced with different words and the captions were applied to several different, not always sexual subjects.

text.visual_description: The image features a character with long hair and a bushy beard, appearing to be in an indoor setting with patterned wallpaper in the background. The main action is a person expressing a reaction, likely speaking or exclaiming.
text.usage_text: "What Year Is It" is the caption of an image macro featuring a photo of Robin Williams' disheveled-looking character from the 1995 film Jumanji. In rage comics, it is often used in a similar fashion to the "my face when" reaction faces to convey the disoriented sense of time experienced when waking up.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a young child energetically running, seemingly startled or excited while holding a yellow bubble wand. The child is captured mid-motion, with one arm outstretched and a lively expression on their face.
text.usage_text: Chubby Bubbles Girl is a Photoshop meme based on a photograph of a girl running through a yard with a bubble maker in her hand. This exploitable series is similar in form to Disaster Girl, Crasher Squirrel, and Thundersnow Ice Cream Cone Guy.

text.visual_description: In the meme template, there are two scenes stacked vertically. The main character, a gray humanoid figure, is depicted in both panels reaching out toward a large yellow circle, which could symbolize something desirable or important.
text.usage_text: Running Away Balloon is a two-panel exploitable webcomic featuring a grey character attempting to reach a yellow balloon but is being held back by a pink character. The meme has been used to express frustrations with the subject's limitations.

text.visual_description: The scene features a woman in a red outfit, standing energetically on a stage. She holds a microphone in her left hand and has both arms stretched wide open with clenched fists, conveying a sense of excitement or announcement.
text.usage_text: Oprah You Get a Car is a series of video remixes and advice animal image macros parodying an episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show in which the entire studio audience is given a free car. Many of the parodies mock the phrase "you get a car," which was repeated by the talk show host several times during the episode.

text.visual_description: The scene centers around a single character with a very distinctive appearance, featuring large, bulging eyes and sparse hair. The character's expression is the focal point, highlighting an intense gaze and an open-mouthed smile that reveals crooked teeth.
text.usage_text: Gollum is a fictional character in the fantasy novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. The character is depicted as a deformed hobbit corrupted by the One Ring, a powerful artifact created by the antagonist Sauron that grants the wearer invisibility.

name: I Too Like To Live Dangerously

text.visual_description: In the scene, the main character is a man wearing a distinctive red suit with a frilly white shirt. He has shaggy hair, wears thick black glasses, and is seated, appearing to engage in conversation.
text.usage_text: I Too Like to Live Dangerously is an advice animal image macro series based on a screencap of the protagonist character and a memorable quote from the 1997 action-comedy film Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery. The captions typically open with descriptions of mildly risky behaviors followed by the phrase “I also like to live dangerously,” in a similar vein to the We've Got a Badass Over Here and Some Men Just Want to Watch the World Burn image macros.

name: Bernie I Am Once Again Asking For Your Support

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image shows an older man wearing a winter coat, standing outdoors on what appears to be a cold day, as indicated by the bare trees and patches of snow. He is looking directly at the camera, seemingly in the midst of speaking.
text.usage_text: I am once again asking for your financial support is a quote uttered by the United States politician Bernie Sanders in his December 2019 fundraising video. Starting in mid-January 2020, the quote gained popularity as an image macro on Reddit and Facebook, with memes imagining various scenarios in which monetary donations are being requested.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a singular character dressed in a distinctive outfit, including a brown top hat and a vibrant purple velvet coat, complemented by a large bowtie and patterned shirt. The character is resting their face on one hand, leaning slightly forward with an expression that suggests attentiveness.
text.usage_text: Condescending Wonka is an advice animals image macro series featuring a screen capture of actor Gene Wilder in the 1971 musical Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory. As its name suggests, the captions can be characterized as patronizing and sarcastic.

text.visual_description: The primary scene features a single character prominently in focus. This figure has a distinct facial expression, with eyes wide open and mouth slightly ajar, gesturing with one hand towards their face.
text.usage_text: Look at me. I'm the captain now. This is a quote from the 2013 movie Captain Phillips, in which an American cargo ship is hijacked by Somali pirates. One of the pirates, taking command of the vessel, delivers the eponymous phrase after storming the bridge and taking the previous captain hostage. The phrase is used online to illustrate a takeover or major change spearheaded by one individual.

text.visual_description: The scene presents a person sitting at a desk holding up an open binder. This individual is dressed in a suit and tie, suggesting a formal or professional setting.
text.usage_text: Donald Trump's First Order of Business is a photoshop meme based on a video clip of United States President Donald Trump holding up an open folder displaying his signature on an executive order.

text.visual_description: The scene features two panels depicting hands holding and interacting with a pill bottle and pills. In the first panel, one hand holds a bottle labeled "Hard to swallow pills" while another hand points to the label.
text.usage_text: Hard to Swallow Pills refers to a series of photoshopped image macros based on two WikiHow stock images: one of someone reading a pill bottle that reads "Hard Pills to Swallow" and the other image of the pills in someone's hands that are labeled a difficult truth. This meme is similar to Pills That Make You Stare and Powder That Makes You Say 'Yes'.

name: Alright Gentlemen We Need A New Idea

text.visual_description: The scene core features a sequence from a four-panel comic format, starring a group of animated, cartoonish businessmen in a corporate meeting room setting. The upper-left panel depicts a serious-looking leader, typically interpreted as a manager or boss, with a furrowed brow and a frown, stating, "Alright gentlemen, we need a new idea." The following panels usually depict brainstorming or presenting suggestions, although the specific suggestions are absent in this template.
text.usage_text: All Right, Gentlemen! (also known as "Alright Gentlemen") is an exploitable comic series illustrating three businessmen's reactions to various proposals. The comic begins with the announcement of a brainstorm session on a video game-related topic, followed by a panel showing an incomplete idea which is met by unimpressed silence and concludes with a panel depicting a slightly improved version of the previous idea that is met with enthusiasm, similar to the format of Reaction Guys comics. The comics are often used to criticize the business practices of video game and tech companies.

text.visual_description: In the image, there is a green, anthropomorphic character dressed in an adventurer's outfit, complete with a large hat and backpack. The character is standing in a cave filled with crystals, and has just opened a treasure chest, exclaiming, "I’ve finally found it… after 15 years." In the next frame, the character holds up a scroll, declaring it to be "The Scroll of Truth!" The third frame shows the scroll unrolled, revealing a blank page.
text.usage_text: The Scroll of Truth is an exploitable image series based on a webcomic by artist Tate Parker, in which an explorer discovers a scroll that provides various unpleasant or unsettling truths, causing him to angrily toss the parchment away.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a single character with long curly hair and a mustache, dressed in what appears to be medieval or fantasy-themed clothing. The person is looking directly at the viewer with an intense gaze.
text.usage_text: "You killed my father, prepare to die" is a phrase from the popular 1987 romantic comedy The Princess Bride. Because the line is repeated so often and has such a strong meaning to one of the characters, it became common for fans to repeat it, especially mockingly before moments of conflict.

text.visual_description: The image shows a girl in the foreground with a puzzled expression and hand gesture typically associated with confusion or questioning. Her hair is tied up and she is wearing a blue top.
text.usage_text: Confused Black Girl, sometimes known as Duh Girl, is an image macro series featuring a teenager with an incredulous expression on her face. The overlaid text generally centers around a frustrating or confounding situation. The meme gained attention when the subject of the photo supposedly sued Instagram after she realized the photo had become a meme.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts two iconic characters, Superman and Batman, in a close-up setting. Superman is on the left, holding a steaming mug, and has a relaxed posture with his arm resting on a surface.
text.usage_text: Keep Calm and Carry On is a catchphrase that originally appeared on a World War II-era British public safety poster. After one of the original posters was recovered and placed in a British bookshop in 2000, the inspirational message was shared online, sparking a series of image macros centered around the phrasal template "Keep Calm and X."

text.visual_description: The scene features a simplistic cartoon character with an exaggeratedly large, round head and a small body, set against a plain background. The character’s facial expression is highly intense, with wide, angry eyes and a mouth open in what appears to be a yell or scream.
text.usage_text: "Y U NO" Guy (also known as "Y U No [X]?") is an image macro series using SMS shorthands and carefree grammar as a way to bring someone's attention to a particular subject or issue. The unique facial expression worn by the stick-figure character is believed to have been traced from the Japanese sci-fi manga/anime series Gantz.

text.visual_description: The image features a historical photograph of a man in an old-fashioned boxing stance with fists raised, typical of late 19th to early 20th-century boxing style. No visible text is present in the image.
text.usage_text: Overly Manly Man is an advice animal type of image macro series featuring a black-and-white photograph of a shirtless, mustachioed man with captions portraying the subject as an overtly masculine alpha male with misogynistic attitudes. The advice animal bears many similarities to other alpha male characters, including Chuck Norris, Vernon Koekemoer, Epic Beard Man, and Technoviking.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template image features a grumpy-looking cat prominently in the foreground, with a partly cloudy sky visible in the background. The cat’s distinct facial expression is central to the image, characterized by downturned features that create an impression of displeasure or annoyance.
text.usage_text: Grumpy Cat is the nickname given to Tardar Sauce, a snowshoe cat that rose to online fame after several pictures of her annoyed facial expressions were posted to Reddit in late September 2012.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a main character at the forefront who is wearing a red and black uniform, reaching out with one hand, his mouth slightly open as if he's speaking or questioning something. In the background, there is another individual in a gold and black uniform, standing with a serious demeanor.
text.usage_text: Annoyed Picard is an image macro series featuring a screen capture of the Star Trek: The Next Generation character Jean-Luc Picard wearing an exasperated expression and captions revealing one's frustration or incredulous reaction accompanied by the rhetorical "how the fuck?", "why the fuck?" or "what the fuck?"

text.visual_description: The image features a single character placed at the center, an older man with gray hair and glasses. There is no specific action taking place, as the character's face is presented in a static and isolated manner.
text.usage_text: High Expectations Asian Father is an advice animal image macro series based on stereotypes and clichés about first-generation Asian parents pushing their children to excel in academic fields in an overbearing manner. Centered around a photograph of a middle-aged Asian man with glasses and grey hair, the captioned image series also went on to inspire a female counterpart advice animal known as Tiger Mom in January 2011.

text.visual_description: The scene features two identical green frog-like puppets facing each other. One appears as the familiar character with visible eyes and a gentle expression, while the other wears a dark hooded cloak and presents a more mysterious demeanor.
text.usage_text: Evil Kermit is a captioned image series featuring a screenshot of the Muppet character Kermit the Frog talking with his nemesis Constantine, dressed as a Sith Lord from Star Wars, who instructs him to perform various indulgent, lazy, selfish, and unethical acts.

text.visual_description: The scene portrays a central character running towards the viewer, with a large group of individuals pursuing them across a shallow body of water. The main character, dressed in pirate attire, appears to be fleeing, emphasizing a sense of urgency and panic.
text.usage_text: Jack Sparrow Run refers to a specific run that Johnny Depp's character Jack Sparrow does in the Pirates of the Caribbean films where he flails his arms wildly to the side as he runs. The run inspired an internet challenge on TikTok in May 2022 during the Amber Heard vs. Johnny Depp trial where users imitate the run in videos.

text.visual_description: The image features a man wearing glasses, sitting at a desk. He is dressed in a light green shirt with a tie.
text.usage_text: Schrute Facts is an image macro series inspired by Dwight Schrute, a character from the American version of the TV sitcom The Office. The overlaid text typically begins with an idiom or common belief, followed by a refutation of the aforementioned idiom based on a rationalist interpretation similar to buzzkill humor.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a young child sitting outdoors on a grassy field, with a serene body of water in the background. The child is wearing a red and white plaid shirt and is positioned towards the camera with their hands clasped together.
text.usage_text: Evil Toddler is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a laughing child with captions describing mischievous pranks and behaviors associated with young children.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single character, a man with braided hair wearing a black shirt and a chain, positioned against a neutral, softly blurred background. The individual is captured mid-laugh, with eyes slightly squinting and mouth open, revealing teeth.
text.usage_text: Yo Dawg, or Sup Dawg, is an image macro series based on portrait shots of American hip hop artist Alvin Nathaniel Joiner, better known by his stage name Xzibit, and humorous captions that are composed around the recursive phrasal template "Yo Dawg, I herd you like (noun X), so I put an (noun X) in your (noun Y) so you can (verb Z) while you (verb Z)." Since rising to popularity in early 2007, the series has been considered one of the most well-known and longest-lasting examples of recursive humor on the Internet.

text.visual_description: The image consists of a series of three panels featuring a dog and a baby sitting side by side on a white wicker chair. The dog appears to be looking at the baby in the first two panels and is seen facing forward in the final panel.
text.usage_text: Dad Joke Dog is an advice animal image macro series featuring a three-image set of a dog and a baby. The first image features the setup of the joke with the dog turned to the baby, the second image features the punchline with the dog turned slightly away, while the third is a reaction shot with both the baby and the dog turned to the camera. The jokes are corny, stereotypical dad jokes similar to those featured on Pun Dog.

text.visual_description: The image is divided into two sequential scenes featuring two main characters. In the first scene, a man in a light-colored suit is seen holding a smoking gun, having seemingly just shot another man, who is slumped motionless in a chair.
text.usage_text: Who Killed Hannibal?, also known as Eric Andre Shooting Hannibal Buress and "Why Would X Do This?", refers to a skit from The Eric Andre Show in which we see Andre fire a gun multiple times at co-host Hannibal Buress, then turn to the camera and ask "Who killed Hannibal?" The scene became an object labeling exploitable image macro in 2018 in which the characters are labeled differently and Andre's line of dialogue is substituted with variations of the phrasal template "Why would X do this?"
